tldr: Apple released a model that reads depth in metres from a single photo or a live camera feed. OpenAI opened its live voice model to app developers, and a quiet call now costs $0.02 a minute instead of $0.05. Google changed how Gemini handles long tool lists, so it only loads a tool's details when the model asks for it. On a new engineering benchmark, Gemini 4 Neon ranks first, ahead of Claude Fable 5.2.

articles.title: Apple's Depth Pro 2 reads metric depth from a photo or live video
articles.summary: Four sizes from 24M to 872M parameters give per-pixel depth in metres that stays steady between frames. Research-only licence.

articles.title: OpenAI opens GPT-Live-1.1 to developers with cheap voice standby
articles.summary: A silent live session now pauses inference at $0.02 a minute instead of $0.05, keeps the connection and resumes with history.

articles.title: Gemini holds tool schemas back until the model asks for them
articles.summary: Tool Retrieval takes 200 tools from 164,000 input tokens to about 23,650, but costs more when schemas repeat against a big context.

articles.title: Gemini 4 Neon tops a new engineering benchmark index at 68.1
articles.summary: The Models Engineering Index ranks 20 models on engineering tasks: Claude Fable 5.2 second at 66.3, GPT-6.2 Astra third at 62.0.
